local_market_longform:
Detroit is its own market, and a cash sale here works differently than the national talking points suggest. Homes in Detroit currently trade around a median of $95,000 and take roughly 38 days to go under contract, with about 41% of area sales closing in cash. When you need certainty instead of a drawn-out listing — a firm number and a date you choose — that local pace is exactly why selling directly makes sense.

The housing stock shapes everything about condition here. Detroit runs heavily to 1900s–1930s brick bungalows, colonials, and two-families, plus post-war frame homes, and each era carries its own repair realities. That matters because we price the house in front of us rather than asking you to renovate it first — the things a traditional buyer's inspector flags are the same things we already expect and account for.

Local conditions are the other factor a generic buyer ignores. Around Detroit, the issues we see most are a large stock of vacant and long-deferred homes, aging century-old plumbing and knob-and-tube wiring, basement flooding, and lead-paint and roof failures. We've made offers on homes with every one of those problems, so none of it scares us off or kills the deal at the last minute.

We buy across the whole area — from close-in neighborhoods like Corktown out to Dearborn and Warren — and in Michigan the local economy anchored by the auto industry and its suppliers, healthcare, and a growing downtown tech and startup scene keeps demand real. Inherited homes, tired rentals, pre-foreclosure situations in Wayne County, and houses that simply need more work than the owner wants to take on: those are the Detroit sellers we help most.

Being a genuinely local buyer near the Renaissance Center also means our offer isn't a lowball pulled from a national algorithm that has never seen Detroit. We know what a block in Corktown, the East Side, Bagley, and Morningside actually sells for, what southeast Michigan buyers will and won't pay for, and how Wayne County's title and closing process really works. That local read is why our sellers get a number they can trust and a closing that actually happens on the date we promised.

situations.title: Facing foreclosure
situations.body: If you're behind on payments in Wayne County, a fast cash sale can settle the loan before it hits your credit. We move on your timeline, not the bank's.

situations.title: Downsizing or aging in place
situations.body: When a longtime Corktown-area home has become too much to keep up, we make a fair offer and let you set a move-out date that isn't rushed.

situations.title: Done being a landlord
situations.body: Problem tenants, deferred maintenance, or a Detroit rental that stopped penciling out. We buy occupied properties and handle the situation so you can walk away clean.

situations.title: Tired of two mortgages
situations.body: If you've already moved and the old Detroit place is just draining you every month, we can take it off your hands quickly.

situations.title: Inherited a house in Detroit
situations.body: Settling an estate — often from out of state — is hard enough without a listing on top of it. We buy inherited Detroit homes as-is, work alongside the Wayne County probate process, and let you take what matters and leave the rest.

situations.title: Relocating
situations.body: A job change shouldn't mean carrying two mortgages or managing a sale from a thousand miles away. Close on your schedule and move on.

faq.q: How fast can you close on my Detroit house?
faq.a: As little as 7 days through a licensed Michigan title company, or any later date you choose. Sellers in Detroit pick the timeline that fits their move.

faq.q: Do I pay any fees or commissions?
faq.a: None. No agent commissions, no listing fees, and we cover standard closing costs. The number we agree on is what you receive.

faq.q: Do I need to repair or clean the house first?
faq.a: No. We buy Detroit homes in any condition — including the a large stock of vacant and long-deferred homes we see so often here. Take what you want and leave the rest.

faq.q: How do you decide the offer amount?
faq.a: We look at recent comparable sales in your Detroit neighborhood — places like Corktown — the home's condition, and current southeast Michigan demand, then make a fair cash offer you're free to accept or decline.

faq.q: Is this a licensed, legitimate way to sell in Michigan?
faq.a: Yes. We are a direct buyer, not your agent or broker, and we put that in writing. Michigan permits direct purchases; we market our own contract interest to a private buyer network and disclose our role in writing.

faq.q: Can you help with foreclosure, probate, or tenants?
faq.a: Often, yes. We regularly work with Wayne County sellers facing foreclosure, probate, liens, or tenant issues, and we structure the sale around the situation.
